verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie; the material advantages are real on both sides and roughly offset. X wins the exhaustiveness axis the brief stresses hardest: it is the only output to find scripts/cloud-retire-terminal.sh:204-207 (K9, the disposition-splitting discharge) and cloud-return.sh:536-537's abandon arm, and the only one to adjudicate the deathwatch from its own code (K11) rather than from other files' prose — I confirmed CUSTODY_BIN appears only at :277 and :282 with no return/abandon in the file. X also verified two assignment sites (NB_ARMED_TARGET at :10728, ENGAGE_VERIFY at :10662) that Y lists as unverified, proved `abandon --stale` has zero callers repo-wide, and found the why-tier.sh:210-212 / validate-bash.sh:633,713 surfaces. Y wins the citation-audit axis the brief also states explicitly, and by a wide margin: it verified all four of the key's M6 stale citations (mailbox-drain :523→8936, :534→7100, :545→7087, wrap-ledger :1018→session-continue:608-612) plus four more I confirmed independently (:12729→4104, :4411→5598-5610, :3558→9064, and cc-custody:22-23's false attribution of the return to sc_announce_before_retire), where X checked only two, neither of them in the key. Y also answered the filename-derivation question from code (sha256 prefix, origin-identity.sh:68-77) that X explicitly left open, stated K8's content-verified condition and :982 precisely where X gave only 'success/landed path', named the session-busy consumer X missed, and produced the single best finding in the set: the custody return at :8707 fires before the SC_DRY exit at :8709 and before the M3 abort at :8754 — I grepped SC_DRY and it is tested at exactly one line, :8709, so a --dry-run self-close really does append a return row against the block's own stated rule. Against that, Y missed two discharge sites and carries one false (though hedged) defect claim, the cloud-ping/slug collision, which the actual openers refute (`cloud-<sid>` vs `cloud/<id>`). Neither output has a single bad citation. No decisive edge either way.

X vs Z — X. Z never located the self-close discharge ('could not locate that code'), so its K6 rests on bin/cc-custody:22-23, the header line whose attribution is itself inaccurate, and it loses the ordering fact (discharge placed after the W3-B1 refusal at :8676-8702); X cites :8657, :8676-8702, :8700 and :8707 and gets it right. Z never read cloud-return, so K8's landed_ok condition, the deliberate 'left $custody OPEN' at :982 and the :537 abandon are all absent; X has both sites. Z missed cloud-retire-terminal entirely, and — on a consumer the brief names by name — says 'I did not find the line that reads it' for operator-readout, where X quotes :915, :929 and :940 correctly. Z's genuine unique wins (the `*)` arm being unreachable because the final else hard-codes `engage_apply_consequences 1 never-engaged` at :13365; the memo key's pane component at :396; the cheap_stamp gap at :1468-1482; the test-suite grounding) are all verified and valuable, but they do not offset four substantive coverage failures against zero bad citations on either side.

Y vs Z — Y. Y's coverage is a near-superset of Z's on everything the brief demanded. Y verified the self-close discharge Z could not find, read cloud-return and stated its condition and its deliberate leave-open, found operator-readout:915 that Z missed, and its citation audit contains Z's two findings (the wrap-ledger→session-continue:608-612 shift and the cc-custody:35-38/44-46 off-by-one) plus the three mailbox-drain citations Z explicitly left unchecked plus four more. Y additionally found the dry-run discharge defect and the terminal-refusal-ignores-custody loop (verified at :4303-4312), neither of which Z has. Z's compensating unique findings — chiefly the `*)` unreachability, which is correct and which Y's table papers over with a '—' in its call-site column — are real but narrower. Both are honest about their limits and neither has a bad citation; Y is simply further along on the same map.
